title: Lipidico Injection Protocol for Serial Crystallography Measurements at the Australian Synchrotron
protocol: Centrifuge the crystal solution gently at 1,000 x g for 10 minutes at 22 °C.
Remove excess buffer to form a soft crystal pellet.
Optimize the ratio of viscous media to crystal volume to maintain high viscosity while increasing crystal concentration.
Set up two 100 µL syringes with a coupler.
Fasten the coupler to the end of the first syringe.
Add 28 µL of crystal solution to the top of the syringe.
Slowly insert the plunger into the top of the syringe.
Gently push the solution down to the end of the coupler tip, removing any air bubbles.
Place one gloved finger on the top of the blunted coupler needle point gently.
Pull the plunger back to draw the solution away from the needle point, generating pressure in the syringe.
Remove the gloved finger quickly to release the pressure and burst air bubbles.
Repeat steps until all bubbles have been removed.
Hold the syringe with the needle facing upwards and the plunger wedged between two fingers.
Quickly rotate the arm holding the syringe 2–3 times in one direction to force out air bubbles.
Inspect the syringe for remaining air bubbles.
Repeat previous steps if any bubbles remain until all air bubbles are removed.
Add ~42 µL of high vacuum silicone grease directly to the top of the second syringe.
Push the plunger all the way down to remove air bubbles and ensure no air gap at the end of the syringe.
Mix crystal solution into the silicone grease by gently depressing the plunger on the crystal solution side.
Push the plunger on the silicone grease side to mix the sample back towards the crystal solution side.
Repeat the mixing process 50 to 100 times until the mixture looks homogeneous.
Visualize the crystals under an optical microscope either through the syringe or, for best results, extract a small amount (~1 μL) on to a glass slide and place a cover slip on top.
Determine crystal concentration by counting the number of crystals in a specific area using the optical microscope images.
Adjust the crystal concentration in the syringe by changing the ratio of crystals to viscous media as needed.
Decrease the amount of silicone grease in step 1.4.
Ensure the viscosity does not fall below 10 Pa.s.
Start with a crystal concentration of 10^9 crystals/mL.
Seal crystals grown in LCP and store them in syringes at room temperature for up to a few days.
Conduct a stability test if crystals are transferred to a different high viscous media.
Determine the stability time limit for data collection based on the test results.
Move all samples into one syringe prior to disconnecting the coupler.
Disconnect the coupler from the syringe.
Attach an injection needle to the syringe.
Screw the needle firmly into the base of the syringe.
Ensure that the needle is fastened tightly to prevent any leakages.
Test the sample stream prior to beam time to select the correct injector needle size.
Mount the injector onto the beamline by removing the cryogenic nozzle and replacing it with the injector.
Loosen the clamping screw holding the cryogenic nozzle and attach the injector to the bracket next to the motorized stage.
Lift the injector from its trolley by holding the black handle.
Place the injector on the motorized stage.
Fasten the black clamping screw knob by hand.
Mount an empty syringe onto the injector.
Select Homing Mode under Tools in the EPOS position control software.
Choose Negative Limit Switch from the options available.
Start Homing and allow the software to run until the screw retracts sufficiently for the syringe to fit.
Stop the homing process when the limit switch is reached automatically if unsupervised.
Mount an empty (‘dummy’) syringe onto the injector by inserting the needle through the slit in the syringe holder.
Line up the syringe against the bracket.
Fasten the syringe with two O-rings.
Wrap the first O-ring across the mid-section of the syringe, attaching it to the hooks on either side.
Loop the second O-ring around the hooks on the upper section and place one part on the top of the glass syringe.
Move the motorized stage with the injector towards the X-ray interaction point via the beamline control software.
Align the needle with the red cross using the inline camera.
Adjust the x position of the stage to align the needle precisely with the X-ray interaction region.
Adjust the y position of the stage to further ensure precise alignment of the needle.
Adjust the z position until the needle tip comes into focus.
Verify alignment of the needle tip and X-ray beam visually by checking that the syringe tip meets the crosshairs visible in the optical microscope image generated by the beamline camera.
Move the needle tip above the cross hairs approximately 100 µm to eliminate x-ray scatter from the needle tip.
Replace the empty syringe with the sample syringe.
Place the injector cap on the sample syringe plunger head.
Move the drive screw to the top of the cap.
In the injector control software, select Velocity Mode.
Input 3000 rpm (~115 nL/s) as the Setting Value and press Apply Setting Value.
Stop the motor when the drive screw touches the cap on the syringe plunger head.
Set the rpm value to zero in the injector control software by changing the Setting Value to ‘0’ as the screw approaches the cap.
Press Apply Setting Value to stop the screw instantly once contact is made.
Gently wiggle the cap to ensure it is firmly held in place.
Change the rpm setting value to 100 after the cap drive screw contacts the plunger top.
Visually inspect the needle tip when the sample first comes out.
Perform a search of the hutch, close the hutch door, and turn on the X-ray beam.
Tune the rpm until a stable stream is generated.
Decrease the rpm setting value to 90.
Repeat step 4.4.1, decreasing the rpm setting value in increments of 10.
For silicone grease, use a value of 30 rpm.
Increase the rpm setting value in increments of 10 until the stream gets straighter.
If the stream does not stabilize even after increasing to 100 rpm, try improving stability using one of the described methods.
Insert a polystyrene sample catcher underneath the sample stream.
Insert a venturi suction funnel into the sample catcher.
Connect the venturi suction funnel to the air outlet tube in the hutch.
Achieve a constant and steady sample flow.
Start data collection once the sample flow is stable.
Optimize the detector distance according to normal X-ray crystallography procedures.
